name: Linux Kernel
summary: A configurable monolithic kernel that exposes process and file abstractions, schedules runnable work, manages memory and devices, and extends the running kernel through modules.

features.name: Virtual filesystem abstraction
features.description: Linux VFS provides a common filesystem interface to userspace and an in-kernel abstraction that allows different filesystem implementations to coexist through objects such as dentries, inodes, files, and superblocks.
benefits: Presents a stable file-oriented interface across filesystem implementations
Allows caching and filesystem-specific operations behind common objects
costs: Indirection and cache coherence add implementation complexity
Filesystem implementations must satisfy VFS locking and lifecycle contracts

features.name: Scheduler classes and runnable work
features.description: The kernel scheduler maintains runnable tasks and selects execution according to scheduler policy and task attributes, with scheduler classes providing policy-specific behavior.
benefits: Supports multiple workload policies including fair, real-time, and deadline scheduling
Separates common scheduling mechanics from policy-specific selection
costs: Latency, fairness, throughput, and energy goals can conflict
Scheduler behavior depends on topology, workload, and configuration

features.name: Kbuild and loadable modules
features.description: Linux uses kbuild to build in-tree and external modules, and module versioning can check exported symbol interfaces before a module is loaded into a kernel build.
benefits: Extends kernel functionality without requiring every feature to be built into the base image
Shares build and symbol compatibility machinery across in-tree and external modules
costs: Module compatibility depends on kernel configuration, headers, and exported symbols
Loading code into the kernel retains the kernel's privilege and failure boundary

features.name: Process and memory resource model
features.description: Linux coordinates user processes, address spaces, file descriptors, and kernel-managed resources through shared kernel objects and system-call boundaries.
benefits: Provides composable process, file, and memory abstractions for applications
Centralizes protection and resource accounting in the kernel
costs: Cross-subsystem synchronization and resource accounting are difficult to reason about
A kernel-wide fault can affect many unrelated processes

mathematical_views.question: How do system calls map process-visible names to shared kernel objects and filesystem-specific operations?
assumptions: Processes, file descriptors, files, dentries, inodes, and superblocks are modeled as typed nodes
Operations traverse object links and dispatch to subsystem implementations
The graph abstracts synchronization details while retaining ownership and lifecycle boundaries

mathematical_views.question: How does runnable work move through scheduling decisions under different scheduler policies?
assumptions: Tasks have runnable, running, blocked, and exited states
Scheduler classes provide policy-dependent selection transitions
The model does not assume a fixed fairness or latency guarantee across configurations

mathematical_views.question: How do kernel configuration, kbuild targets, exported symbols, and modules define an extensible runtime boundary?
assumptions: Build configuration determines which code and interfaces exist
A module's imported symbols must satisfy the selected kernel ABI checks
The graph describes extension capability and compatibility constraints, not module safety

benefits: Uniform file API with interchangeable filesystem implementations
costs: Common object and locking contracts increase subsystem complexity
Policy interactions make performance and latency less predictable

benefits: Configurable images and post-build extension points
costs: Version, configuration, and symbol compatibility must be maintained

benefits: Strong central protection boundary and reusable process abstractions
costs: Kernel-wide coupling raises the impact of subsystem defects
